title: herdrdev/herdr
lede: herdr is a terminal workspace for coding agents: a single Rust binary that keeps agent sessions running in a background server and shows which panes are working, blocked or idle.

points: Closing the client or dropping an SSH connection leaves terminals running; after a restart it restores the layout and can resume supported agent sessions.
Every pane is marked working, blocked or idle, so an agent waiting for an answer is easy to find.
Agents can drive herdr through its CLI and socket API to open panes, prompt one another and wait on a blocked agent.
It runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and others in their own terminals rather than wrapping them.
Local work and saved SSH machines share one window, with tmux-style keys, mouse support and plugins.
